hook: A 13.46‑meter TBM bored a tunnel under the Panama Canal.

sections.voiceover: A 13.46‑meter TBM bored a tunnel under the Panama Canal.
sections.visual_cue: Show the 13.46‑meter Herrenknecht Mixshield TBM named Panamá.

sections.voiceover: On Oct 26 2026, TBM Panamá completed a 4.5 km drive. How did a 13.46‑meter machine bore such a long underground passage?
sections.visual_cue: Map of the Panama Canal highlighting the route from Farfán to Albrook.

sections.voiceover: Except the machine was built by Herrenknecht, a German tunnelling specialist.
sections.visual_cue: Display the Herrenknecht logo with a German engineering badge.

sections.voiceover: The Mixshield TBM Panamá, 13.46 m in diameter, powered the entire 4.5 km excavation. César Pinzón of Metro de Panamá confirmed the milestone for Line 3.
sections.visual_cue: Animated line showing 4.5 km tunnel progress ending at Albrook on Oct 26 2026.

sections.voiceover: A 13.46‑meter machine carved Panama’s first canal tunnel.
sections.visual_cue: Close‑up of TBM Panamá with overlay ‘13.46 m diameter’.
